plan.angle: Title: 'Can Semaglutide (Wegovy, Ozempic) Affect Eyesight? What EMA Says About NAION #shorts'. Within 10s: Europe's regulator lists NAION as a very rare possible side effect, affecting up to 1 in 10,000 people on semaglutide. As of Oct 2026, US labels don't list it and FDA says it is evaluating. Studies disagree on cause. Shared risk factors: diabetes, high blood pressure, sleep apnea. Sudden vision change: same-day urgent care, tell your prescriber, don't stop on your own. Exact prescriber line.
plan.working_title: Can Semaglutide (Wegovy) Cause Vision Loss? What Regulators Say #shorts
plan.why: Rising fear-driven searches (KXAN/Yahoo, Oct 5) where law-firm pages dominate the results. It's a safety question with a named drug and a regulator's number. This is a caution topic, so the angle is evidence-first; it's today's myth-busting slot. | fact-check: Verified: EMA's PRAC concluded in June 2025 that NAION is a 'very rare' side effect of semaglutide (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy), affecting up to 1 in 10,000 people (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/news/prac-concludes-eye-condition-naion-very-rare-side-effect-semaglutide-medicines-ozempic-rybelsus-wegovy). The EMA says observational studies in adults with type 2 diabetes suggest about a 2-fold relative risk, roughly 1 extra case per 10,000 person-years. FDA status: a 29 Sep 2026 report says US labels for Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus and Mounjaro still don't list NAION, and FDA lists it as a potential signal it is 'evaluating' (https://www.medicaldaily.com/fda-glp1-naion-signal-us-label-warning-review-479225). That is a secondary source, so hedge it. Fixes: (1) Never say 'FDA warning'. Say 'as of Oct 2026, US labels don't list NAION; FDA says it is evaluating'. (2) I couldn't verify the Austin father's story. Drop it or mention it generically ('recent news reports'), with no names and no dramatised imagery. (3) Keep the claim to semaglutide only; the EMA ruling doesn't cover tirzepatide. (4) Say 'linked to' or 'listed as a possible very rare side effect', not 'causes'. (5) Don't paraphrase the EMA's 'stop if confirmed' line as viewer advice; that's the doctor's decision. Red flag: sudden vision loss means same-day urgent care (911/999 if sudden and severe). Don't stop the medicine on your own.

factcheck.summary:
I checked every factual claim against its source, and they all hold up. EMA/PRAC (June 2025) concluded that NAION is a very rare side effect of semaglutide (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy), meaning it may affect up to 1 in 10,000 people. Large epidemiological studies in type 2 diabetes found roughly double the risk, about 1 extra case per 10,000 person-years. The EMA ruling covers semaglutide only.

The FDA's Oct–Dec 2024 signals page lists NAION as a potential signal across GLP-1 receptor agonists, tirzepatide included, and says "FDA is evaluating the need for regulatory action". Medical Daily (29 Sept 2026) reports that US labels still don't list NAION. The script correctly says "reportedly" and gives the date, so that time-sensitive claim is hedged properly.

The American Academy of Ophthalmology lists diabetes, high blood pressure and sleep apnea among the risk factors. NHS says to call 999 or go to A&E if you suddenly can't see from 1 or both eyes.

The framing is good:
- The relative risk sits next to the absolute number.
- The studies are labelled as observational and limited to type 2 diabetes.
- The script doesn't claim tirzepatide causes NAION.
- The exact prescriber line is there.
- The triage is sensible.

There are three minor wording issues, each with a fix below. None of them changes the verdict.

issues.claim: For other sudden vision changes, get urgent care the same day.
issues.problem: NHS doesn't say 'same day'. For vision changes that aren't an emergency, it advises an urgent GP appointment or NHS 111. EMA says to see your doctor promptly. The wording is a small paraphrase that the source doesn't support.
issues.fix: Narration: "If you suddenly can't see from one or both eyes, call 911 or 999, or go to the ER or A&E. For other sudden vision changes, get urgent medical advice. Tell your prescriber; don't stop the medicine on your own." On-screen list item 2: "Other sudden changes: urgent medical advice"

issues.claim: Tell your prescriber; don't stop the medicine on your own.
issues.problem: EMA says semaglutide must be stopped if NAION is confirmed. The script is right to say 'don't stop on your own', but leaving out that a clinician will stop it once NAION is confirmed weakens the EMA guidance slightly.
issues.fix: Replace the last sentence with: "Tell your prescriber. If NAION is confirmed, they'll stop semaglutide. Don't stop it on your own."

issues.claim: On-screen: "~2× risk ≈ 1 extra case per 10,000 person-years"
issues.problem: The main on-screen line leaves out the population (type 2 diabetes) and the observational design. Only the small stat label carries them, so the headline text is broader than the narration.
issues.fix: On-screen text: "Type 2 diabetes studies (observational): ~2× risk ≈ 1 extra case per 10,000 person-years"
